title: Can Agentic Code Review Catch Vulnerabilities Before They Are Merged?
abstract: arXiv:2610.33509v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: LLM agents have been increasingly adopted for security-focused code review, but existing benchmarks mostly derive the reviewed changes from their later fixes instead of the real-world bug-introducing commits. In this paper, we present SecPRBench, the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating agentic security review on validated real-world code changes. More specifically, we have built an automated agentic pipeline to autonomously harvest, build, and validate massive real-world bug-introducing commits for popular software systems. To ensure precise evaluation, we also adopt LLM-as-a-judge to credit the findings matching ground-truth vulnerabilities. To date, we have collected 265 tasks from nine critical systems, including Firefox, V8, and OpenSSL with millions of lines of code. tldr: 提出了SecPRBench——首个基于经过验证的真实漏洞引入提交来评估智能体安全代码审查的综合性基准，涵盖Firefox、V8、OpenSSL等九个关键系统的265个任务，并发现八个前沿模型的召回率仅为32.5%至78.1%。
